messages:
lisa_cs: FYI escalated from MediBank — end-of-day batch blew past expected load and their dedicated pool didn't scale, customers saw 429s and long-tail latencies. attaching what they sent.

emma_support: thanks, adding @raj oncall. any SLO breaches or billing blocks?

raj_oncall: saw a spike around 22:13 UTC, a lot of 429s reported by the frontend. backend logs show multiple 'attach timeout' and 'FailedScheduling'. can you paste the customer's repro?

customer_medi: our nightly ETL kicks at 22:00 and opens ~500 concurrent streams. we expect autoscale to add workers. instead we got ~30% of expected capacity and 429s for ~18 minutes. kube events show `pod unschedulable: node(s) had taints` and our logs show the runtime returned 429/503.

sre_matt: interesting — we recently shipped reserved-burst fast-path which taints nodes to reserve capacity during warmup. if pods don't have the matching toleration they won't schedule. do the dedicated runtime pods carry tolerations?

devex_jamie: admission is supposed to inject tolerations for dedicated pods, but there's a flag controlling fast-path behavior. current operator config snippet (from cluster):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  enable_reserved_burst: "true"
  reserved_burst_taint: "reserved-burst=true:NoSchedule"
  fastpath_enabled: "true"
```

emma_support: customer's repro steps they shared: 
1) POST /v1/generate with customer key (they provided a redacted sample)
2) fire 500 concurrent requests over ~10s
3) after ~90s, requests begin failing with 429, and queue depth grows
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d @payload.json

raj_oncall: can infra run `kubectl describe nodes` and `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide` and grep for taints/events and paste a snippet?

infra-bot: executed commands, returning trimmed output:
```
Node/node-37 Taints: reserved-burst=true:NoSchedule
Pods Pending: 7  Reason: Unschedulable
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  0s  7/50 nodes are available: 50 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

sre_matt: that matches hypothesis — pods lacked the toleration. root cause could be an admission regression, operator flag change, or image change that removed toleration injection. explains the ~18 minute stall while nodes were tainted.

lisa_cs: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they can't wait another nightly window. what's fastest?

sre_matt: two quick mitigations: (A) disable reserved-burst/fastpath so nodes stop being tainted, (B) patch the pod spec to include tolerations so they schedule on reserved nodes. (A) is lower risk for immediate recovery.

devex_jamie: I can flip the operator flag to disable fastpath (configmap) which will stop new nodes from being tainted; controller reconciliation will take ~30s and existing tainted nodes will be drained of the taint shortly after.

infra-bot: applying config change now: set `fastpath_enabled=false` at 23:02 UTC. Controller reconciling.

raj_oncall: watching scheduling events and metrics — pending pods count dropping, new pods becoming Running. latency and error rate trending down.

customer_medi: we saw throughput recover around 23:06 UTC, thanks. can you confirm timeline and next steps to prevent recurrence?

sre_matt: preliminary RCA: runtime image v2.4.1 had a regression that skipped toleration injection when the operator flag fastpath=true due to a changed admission hook ordering. PR #5823 fixes injection and adds e2e to assert tolerations. we'll push a patch and schedule a follow-up rollout.

lisa_cs: filing CS follow-up ticket CS-7892. customer updated with timeline, mitigation taken, and promise of postmortem.

emma_support: action item: add a preflight check to the feature gate rollout that validates pod tolerations against any node taints introduced by reserved-burst. also add a runbook entry: if reserved-burst is enabled, verify `kubectl describe nodes | grep Taints` and `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.tolerations}'` before enabling.

devex_jamie: will add gating to rollout pipeline and an automated test to the operator repo to catch missing tolerations. creating follow-up ticket ENG-12045. :white_check_mark:

lisa_cs: customer satisfied with immediate mitigation, will await the postmortem. closing loop here after ENG patch and CS update.

emma_support: thanks everyone — leaving notes for oncall handover. :thumbsup:
